Localtify 0.5.0 is a major update from 0.4.1: an experimental Android companion, connected playback, richer library navigation, smarter playlists and discovery, lyrics and scrobbling, safer library tools, and a broad UI/performance cleanup.

## Downloads

- **Windows x64:** `localtify-setup-0.5.0.exe`.
- **Linux x64:** AppImage, Debian (`.deb`) and RPM packages.
- **Android:** `localtify-0.5.0-android.apk`, signed with the dedicated Localtify Android release key. Requires Android 7.0/API 24 or later and an up-to-date System WebView.
- **Verification:** `SHA256SUMS` covers every installer and updater asset. The desktop packages are not code-signed; operating-system trust warnings may appear.

## Android companion and connected playback

- Pair your phone with the desktop app over home Wi-Fi, copy music and artwork, and listen offline from phone storage. Likes, playlists, play counts and listening history sync both ways.
- Phone navigation includes customizable bottom tabs, a mini player, a full-screen player with lyrics and queue access, swipe-to-skip, system media controls and native Back handling.
- Resume interrupted transfers, skip unchanged files and retry batches without counting the same plays twice. Temporarily unavailable desktop audio no longer causes the phone's cached library to be treated as deleted.
- While both devices are connected, share live likes, playback status and progress; control play/pause, next/previous and seeking from either device; edit the shared queue; and use **Play on** to move playback with its position and queue.
- Desktop-backed lyrics, biographies and recommendation results can be cached for offline use after fetching. Imports, tagging, cover editing and library maintenance remain desktop tools.

## Library, collections and navigation

- Dedicated **Artists** and **Genres** views make local metadata browsable, including featured artist credits and multi-value genre tags.
- Albums, artists, genres, playlists and Daily Mixes open as consistent collection pages with Back/Forward history, shared play/shuffle/queue actions and context menus. Album details open directly rather than being buried below a long shelf.
- Sort the library by artist. Sort genres by tracks, artists, plays, recent additions or name, and filter out genres with only a few tracks; choices are remembered.
- Folder imports prefer useful embedded album metadata. Large-library artwork handling and cover readiness are more reliable, including when the playing song is refreshed.
- Analytics now derives library health from the current songs and missing-file state rather than a stale snapshot.

## Playlists, discovery and local audio analysis

- **Smart playlists** fill themselves from rules for metadata, likes, play/finish/skip counts and listening dates, with all/any matching, ordering, limits and presets.
- **Recommended songs** appear under regular playlists, with add and refresh controls. They use saved audio analysis when available, or library relationships such as shared artists, genres, albums and playlists.
- **Playlists from a prompt** understand supported artists, genres, exclusions, listening-history filters and requested sizes. Optional local sound matching uses a separately enabled model download; preview and deselect songs before saving or playing.
- Opt-in, on-device audio analysis powers **Similar songs**, group recommendations from playlists/liked songs/recent listening, and **Song Radio** when your queue ends. Artist variety, skips, genre overlap and repeated back-to-back listening inform the results.
- Daily Mixes have more stable grouping, genre-aware names, listening feedback and rotation to reduce repetition. **Not for me** controls exclude unwanted songs and artists from recommendations while leaving normal library playback available.
- **Discover** uses optional Last.fm lookups for artists and songs outside your library, with a deliberate handoff to Downloads. Artist pages can show Last.fm biographies with cached offline fallback and source attribution. This is discovery, not an in-app streaming catalog.

## Lyrics, scrobbling, downloads and library tools

- Experimental synchronized lyrics support local `.lrc` files, optional online lookup, manual LRCLIB matching, offline persistence and per-song timing offsets.
- Connect **Last.fm and ListenBrainz** for eligible scrobbles, now-playing updates, queued offline submissions and deliberate history submission. Phone listening can be submitted through the paired desktop.
- **Watched folders** import newly added music automatically, including subfolders, with status and manual checking controls.
- **Duplicate review** uses album-aware grouping, explicit merge choices, database backups and file-safety protections rather than automatically deleting matches.
- Experimental **MusicBrainz tagging** audits missing/inconsistent tags, proposes metadata and cover art, and writes accepted changes only after review. Album completion tools help find missing tracks.
- YouTube downloads prefer proper audio-only streams instead of falling back to low-quality muxed video. Quality/format options reach the downloader correctly, and **Keep original audio** avoids a second lossy encode.
- macOS yt-dlp selection is fixed, and public Spotify imports handle missing artist metadata more reliably.

## Home, player and platform polish

- Reorder, hide, show and reset Home sections. Added shelves include Daily Mixes, Recently played and New albums, with optional Liked songs, Rediscover and Not played yet.
- Player title/artist links, like actions, the queue panel, album repeat-all, sidebar tab customization and the idle-screensaver toggle make common controls easier to reach.
- Android draws edge-to-edge behind the system bars with safe-area padding. Home is less cluttered, collection controls fit narrow screens, and song rows leave more room for titles while retaining touch-sized actions.
- Home and collection heroes use dim, blurred album artwork with GIF support. Settings, theme surfaces, menus, dialogs, focus restoration, long labels and playlist-row positioning receive consistency and accessibility fixes.
- macOS gains native window controls and a standard menu bar with keyboard shortcuts. These source/runtime improvements are included; this release publishes installers for Windows, Linux and Android.

## Performance, maintenance and validation

- Reuse normalized search text and existing index lookups, avoid unnecessary artist/album recounts, and cache repeated artist/genre calculations within each recommendation request.
- In the final optimization pass, a synthetic 50,000-song fixture measured metadata-equivalent snapshot indexing at **2.11 seconds → 165 ms**, and recommendation scoring at **279 → 117 ms**, with matching results. These are local processing measurements, not whole-app latency guarantees.
- Reduce repeated work in library updates, Home shelves, cover selection, download matching and phone artwork swipes. Remove unused components/helpers/exports, obsolete CSS/keyframes/theme variables and stale audit documents.
- Strengthen Electron renderer sandboxing, Content Security Policy, IPC/navigation boundaries, bridge typing and feature ownership. Database migration, backup and recovery checks remain part of validation.
- Experimental Rust-kernel tooling remains opt-in with JavaScript fallback; standard desktop installers exclude the optional addon. Compatible dependency updates resolve the previously identified critical npm advisories; remaining findings are listed below.
- Validation includes **517 automated tests**, release/performance checks, Windows/Linux installer and native CI, Android release build/lint/unit checks, package-format checks, updater-hash checks and all nine published asset digests. The public APK's checksum and dedicated release certificate were verified.

## Android installation and updating

Install the APK, then pair it with the same desktop version through **Settings → Library**. Keep both devices on a trusted home network during sync; cached audio plays offline afterwards. See the [Android guide](https://github.com/meshahid973/localitfy/blob/v0.5.0/docs/android.md).

An existing debug APK has a different signing key and cannot be updated directly with this release APK. Sync pending phone changes back to the desktop and preserve anything you need before uninstalling the debug build; uninstalling removes its local data. Future official APK updates use the same dedicated release key.

## Known limitations

- Android remains experimental. Sync/live transfers use plain HTTP on the trusted home network; do not expose the sync port to the internet.
- A delayed handoff acknowledgement can supersede a newer playback session. Select the intended device again if playback switches unexpectedly.
- Real-device background/Doze, headset controls, older WebViews and installed-desktop migration testing are not comprehensive.
- The pre-release full npm audit reported one high Electron entry and six moderate packaging/minimatch entries. The runtime-only audit reported zero; Electron provides the shipped browser runtime despite its devDependency classification. These advisories remain unresolved in this release.
- Online integrations are optional and may send the corresponding metadata or listening submissions to their providers; local audio analysis runs on-device.

# Localtify 0.4.1 🎧

0.4.1 is a hotfix and stability update after the big 0.4.0 release.
This update focuses on fixing Linux update behavior, improving Spotify playlist downloads, and cleaning up a few important issues that showed up after release.

0.4.0 was a huge polish update, but 0.4.1 is about making that release safer and more reliable for real users, especially on Linux AppImage builds.

## Changelog ✨

### 🐧 Linux updater behavior fixed

Linux AppImage updates are now handled more safely.

Previously, Linux builds could detect an update and cause weird startup/load issues, especially when older AppImages like 0.3.8 or 0.4.0 saw a newer release. That was not acceptable because older versions should still open normally.

For now, Linux AppImage updates are manual-only:

* Linux no longer auto-downloads AppImage updates.
* Linux no longer auto-installs or replaces the running AppImage.
* Linux update checks now show that an update exists.
* The update action opens the GitHub release page instead.
* This prevents old Linux AppImages from breaking during startup.
* Windows auto-update behavior is unchanged.

This is a safer Linux update flow until AppImage auto-update is fully reliable.

### 🎵 Spotify playlist/download improvements

Spotify playlist handling has been improved, especially when Spotify only provides weak public playlist metadata.

Changes include:

* Improved Spotify-to-YouTube matching logic.
* Added more fallback search attempts for Spotify tracks.
* Added a direct search fallback when safe candidate matching cannot find results.
* Reduced instant “Could not safely match this Spotify track” failures.
* Improved handling for tracks where public Spotify fallback does not include proper artist data.
* Improved Spotify download messages so failed matches are easier to understand.
* Fixed cases where a track could fail before yt-dlp even had a chance to search properly.

Spotify downloads should now be less strict and more useful while still trying to avoid completely wrong matches.

### 📁 Album import fixes

Album importing was improved after users found that importing a folder with many albums could group everything incorrectly.

Fixes include:

* Fixed recursive album folder detection.
* Prevented parent folders from becoming one giant album.
* Improved album detection for folders containing multiple separate albums.
* Improved folder-based album titles.
* Improved handling for artist folders containing album folders.
* Added better behavior for re-importing album folders.
* Reduced duplicate/stale album entries after re-imports.

This should make large album folder imports behave much more naturally.

### 🗑️ Album actions and cleanup

Album management received some small but important cleanup.

Added/improved:

* Delete selected album actions.
* Delete all albums action.
* Safer confirmation before clearing albums.
* Cleaner album import status messages.
* Better empty album states.
* Less clutter when no albums exist.
* Better handling for generated/custom/folder/tag albums.

Album pages should now feel less messy and easier to manage.

### 🔁 Repeat-one playback fix

Fixed an issue where repeat-one could play another song instead of restarting the current song.

Changes include:

* Repeat-one now restarts the same track properly.
* Crossfade/preload behavior no longer steals playback from repeat-one.
* End-of-track handling is safer for looped songs.

### 🎨 Custom theme persistence

Fixed an issue where custom theme settings could disappear after updating.

Changes include:

* Custom theme settings are backed up locally.
* Custom theme colors are restored after app updates.
* App update/default settings migrations should no longer wipe custom theme choices.

### 🎛️ Player and UI polish

Small player and UI fixes were added after 0.4.0.

Changes include:

* Improved play/pause morph button behavior.
* Improved player button sizing.
* Improved repeat/shuffle icon polish.
* Improved queue/player badge alignment.
* Reduced some expensive player blur/glow behavior.
* Reduced unnecessary progress-related re-rendering.
* Improved player performance while music is playing.

### 🚀 Performance and stability

0.4.1 includes smaller stability fixes after the large 0.4.0 performance work.

Changes include:

* Reduced unnecessary renderer update work.
* Improved progress update timing.
* Reduced player visual cost in heavier states.
* Improved Linux startup safety.
* Improved packaged build behavior.
* Improved main/preload bridge reliability.
* Reduced risk from Linux updater behavior.

### 🪟 Windows

Windows update behavior remains normal.

Windows still supports the normal installer/update metadata flow through:

* `localtify-setup-0.4.1.exe`
* `localtify-setup-0.4.1.exe.blockmap`
* `latest.yml`

### 🐧 Linux release note

Linux AppImage users should download updates manually from GitHub releases.

Linux release should include:

* `localtify-0.4.1-x86_64.AppImage`

Linux release should not include `latest-linux.yml` for now, because Linux AppImage auto-update is disabled until it is fully safe.

## Thank you 💖

Thank you to everyone using Localtify and testing the app across Windows and Linux.

0.4.1 is not meant to be a huge feature update. It is a safety and reliability patch to make the 0.4.0 release better for real users.

The goal is still the same: make Localtify feel like a cute, smooth, reliable local music library app.

# Localtify 0.3.9

Localtify 0.3.9 is a quick stability update focused on fixing the bugs that made 0.3.8 feel rough in real use.

This is not a huge feature release. It is mainly here to clean up the important stuff before 0.4.0.

## What changed

### Spotify imports are safer now

This update improves the Spotify import flow so Localtify is less likely to grab the wrong song with the same or similar name.

Before, Spotify metadata could look correct in the app, but the downloaded audio underneath could still be a random matching result. 0.3.9 makes the matching stricter and keeps Spotify tracks tied to their proper import result more reliably.

### Song editing is back in the right-click menu

Thanks to @Void-gg7 for reporting that song names and artists could not be edited properly anymore.

The right-click menu now has **Edit song data** again, so you can edit the song title, artist, and album from inside Localtify.

For now, the broken cover actions were removed from the right-click menu so the menu only shows actions that actually work properly. Cover tools will get a cleaner rebuild later in 0.4.0.

### Local album importing is more reliable

Thanks to Crocodile73 for asking about local album importing.

The album buttons have been fixed so adding albums and importing album folders actually opens the proper folder/import flow again.

### Missing library files are easier to clean up

The Library now properly shows songs that still exist in Localtify but are missing from disk.

You can switch to the missing-files view and remove broken entries from the library without touching real music files that still exist.

### Feedback now works properly

0.3.9 adds a working feedback popup so users can report bugs or send suggestions more easily.

You can open it by typing:

```txt
/feedback
```

or:

```txt
feedback
```

The feedback system can send reports to a Discord webhook when configured by the app build.

### Analytics cleanup

Analytics were cleaned up to feel less invasive.

Removed from analytics:

* screen bucket
* CPU thread bucket
* device memory bucket
* timezone/local-time style tracking

Country/region-level locale info is still kept so it is possible to understand where users are roughly using Localtify from without collecting unnecessary device details.

### Security and CodeQL fixes

0.3.9 also fixes some security/check issues:

* replaced weak random ID fallback in analytics
* cleaned up Discord feedback webhook handling
* improved packaged `.env` loading for feedback builds
* fixed broken CSS selector issues in settings

## UI polish

A few small UI problems were cleaned up too:

* cleaner Library missing-files section
* better spacing in the Library area
* cleaner song context menu
* improved feedback popup styling
* fixed ugly text glyphs in buttons
* improved edit song modal controls

## Credits

Thanks to everyone who reported bugs and rough edges.

Special thanks to:

* Void-gg7 for reporting the missing song data editing flow
* @yudafao for reporting the Spotify song name problem

0.4.0 will focus more on bigger polish, better cover editing, and cleaner feature work. This release is mainly here to make the current app more stable.

# Localtify 0.3.8 — Stability & Polish Update 🎧

Localtify 0.3.8 is a cleanup, stability, and release-quality update focused on making the big 0.3.7 foundation feel finished. This release polishes Albums V2, improves playback/download reliability, cleans up settings and visuals, and makes the Linux release feel more official.

## Main Highlights ✨

### Albums V2 Polish

* Improved the Albums section so custom albums feel more built into the app.
* Cleaned up album shelves, album cards, spacing, and detail page behavior.
* Improved album cover handling and custom cover display reliability.
* Polished album actions so managing local albums feels smoother and less patched together.

### Playback & Audio Stability

* Improved the playback engine for more reliable daily listening.
* Cleaned up volume behavior and faster volume setting changes.
* Added more stability around background audio and saved playback settings.
* Improved missing-file recovery behavior so broken library entries are easier to handle.
* Reduced chances of playback breaking because of stale or missing local file paths.

### Downloads & Import Reliability

* Improved YouTube/download flow reliability for local music importing.
* Kept the main YouTube-to-audio feature intact while cleaning the surrounding release behavior.
* Improved download settings copy and folder handling.
* Cleaned up failed/finished download behavior so the app feels less messy after use.

### Metadata & Cover Tools

* Added/cleaned cover metadata tools for missing covers.
* Improved metadata cleaner preview behavior.
* Added safer actions for cleaning selected metadata.
* Added undo support around recent metadata cleaning work.
* Improved cover cache handling and missing-cover filtering.

### Settings Cleanup

* Reworked the settings pages into a cleaner, calmer layout.
* Removed unfinished or confusing controls that were not properly wired.
* Cleaned up Appearance, Library, Downloads, Covers, Updates, About, and Advanced sections.
* Removed old broken settings hero/card clutter.
* Made settings feel more like a real app page instead of a pile of patches.

### Theme & Visual Polish

* Cleaned up theme handling and custom theme behavior.
* Improved live theme editing so color changes feel faster and less laggy.
* Reduced visual replay/animation lag while editing settings.
* Cleaned up theme variables and release-safe styling.
* Removed hidden/old background styling that caused visual conflicts.
* Kept the app dark, solid, and readable instead of relying on unstable transparency tricks.

### Sidebar & Navigation Polish

* Reworked sidebar styling to be more stable and release-safe.
* Added cleaner sidebar icon motion and a Discord-style active indicator.
* Removed broken hover-shift behavior that caused layout problems.
* Improved sidebar readability and reduced CSS conflicts.
* Made the sidebar feel more consistent across Home, Library, Albums, Settings, and other pages.

### Onboarding Improvements

* Updated onboarding visuals and theme icons.
* Cleaned up the onboarding logo/title layout.
* Improved first-run styling so the app starts cleaner for new users.
* Kept onboarding lightweight and more polished without turning it into a full redesign.

### Cat Buddy Polish 🐾

* Added and refined the small cat buddy feature.
* Improved sprite animation handling.
* Fixed direction/movement behavior across multiple passes.
* Cleaned up the cat buddy styling so it works better with the release-safe UI.

## Linux Release Improvements 🐧

* Prepared Localtify 0.3.8 for Linux AppImage release.
* Updated Linux install copy to match the 0.3.8 AppImage name.
* Fixed Linux build problems caused by Windows `node_modules`.
* Confirmed Fedora needs a fresh Linux clone/build folder instead of building from `/run/media/...`.
* Fixed Linux release icon problems by generating proper `build/icon.png` and `build/icon.ico`.
* Built the Linux AppImage successfully as:

`localtify-0.3.8-x86_64.AppImage`

* Published the Windows build for Localtify 0.3.8.
* Updated the version flow so the TypeScript app version matches `package.json`.
* Refreshed the `v0.3.8` tag so the release points to the correct latest commit.

## Version & Release Fixes 🛠️

* Updated the app’s internal TypeScript version from `0.3.7` to `0.3.8`.
* Updated the in-app “What’s New” changelog from old 0.3.6 text to proper 0.3.8 release notes.
* Updated shared constants/types/utils comments to match the 0.3.8 release pass.

* Matched the app version with `package.json` so the release does not show mixed versions.

## Performance & Stability

* Reduced heavy pointer/proximity motion on large lists and cards.
* Kept motion focused on sidebar, player, and hero controls.
* Improved library performance by keeping heavy reductions in the worker.
* Reduced CSS conflicts from old App/Core/Home/Settings patches.
* Removed unstable transparent/acrylic-style behavior from the release-safe build.
* Improved overall UI consistency across the main app shell.

### What changed in v0.3.7

Big changes here. Linux is now supported, and the main new feature is the new album section, suggested in the Issues area by @Crocodile73.

Some performance changes have also been made, and the onboarding has been fully rewritten for new users.

### New features

Added a new Albums section.
